factory_wide_operational_requirements: AUDIT ARTIFACT PLACEMENT (applies to every core-lane and Frontier independent audit). The gate reader runs `jq -e '.gate=="PASS" or .gate=="REVISE" or .gate=="BLOCKED"' results/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_GATE.json` against the AUDIT JOB CHECKOUT, i.e. the repository root you are currently in. Write results/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_<run_id>_GATE.json and reports/audit/<lane>/CYCLE_<run_id>.md there, using exactly those relative paths from your current working directory. Do NOT write them into /tmp/lex_team (the producer worktree): artifacts left there are invisible to the gate reader, the audit job fails with `jq: error: Could not open file ...`, no promotion happens and the lane re-dispatches forever. Verified this cycle: runs 38571087814 and 38578725589 failed this way; run 38559540834 passed when the same auditor used relative paths. This is a file-location contract only — the gate verdict stays fully independent.

DIRECTOR BASE-SHA GUARD MISFIRES ON REPAIR RUNS (control-plane hardening item; .github/** is control-plane scope and is NOT edited from here). factory-director.yml records reports/director/BASE_DIRECTION_SHA_<run>.txt at the 'Record control-plane base' step AFTER 'Restore exact rejected proposal for repair', so on a repair run the recorded base is the REJECTED PROPOSAL's direction sha rather than main's. Verified in run 38786736419: the workflow-recorded value was 02351c26... (rejected proposal v52) while origin/main:state/factory_direction.json is 52f704ed... (v51, unchanged since run 38784614826 recorded exactly that value). On a PASS the integrate job compares the recorded base with main's current sha and would therefore skip integration with a spurious 'Superseded Director proposal' warning for EVERY repair round. Intended fix (owner/control-plane maintainer): record the base before restoring the rejected proposal, or inherit origin/<rejected-run>/reports/director/BASE_DIRECTION_SHA_<rejected-run>.txt on repair runs. Route-around used this round: the repair republished the TRUE control-plane base (52f704ed...) in its own BASE file and discloses both values in reports/director/RUN_38786736419.md; the supersession check still works as designed because main had not moved.
